knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

```{r load_packages, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Introduction

This analysis checks how well the fine-tuned PubMedBERT model picks out
cohort names from article text. It compares the model's predicted
entities with the hand-annotated (true) entities in the validation set
in two ways:

1. **Entity-level, per paper:** precision, recall and F1 for cohort
   names, based on the set of distinct entities found in each paper.
2. **Token-level confusion matrix:** how often each true entity class is
   predicted as each class, across all entity types.

# Entity-level performance (per paper)

## Load validation predictions

```{r load_predictions}
# One row per sentence in the validation set, with true and predicted
# entities stored as ";"-separated strings
preds <- data.table::fread(
  here::here("output/text_mining_predictions/validation_entity_predictions.csv")
)
```

## Reshape to one row per entity

```{r reshape_entities}
ents <-
  preds |>
  # entity columns only, not the start / end positions
  select(pubmed_id, predicted_cohorts, true_cohorts) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("predicted_cohorts", "true_cohorts"),
    names_to = "col",
    values_to = "ent"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(ent)) |>
  # split ";"-separated entities into separate rows
  separate_rows(ent, sep = ";") |>
  mutate(
    # "true" or "predicted"
    source = str_extract(col, "^(true|predicted)"),
    # entity type, e.g. "predicted_cohorts" -> "cohort"
    type   = str_remove(str_remove(col, "^(true|predicted)_"), "s$"),
    # normalise case / whitespace so near-identical strings match
    ent    = str_squish(str_to_lower(ent))
  ) |>
  filter(ent != "") |>
  # count each entity once per paper
  distinct(pubmed_id, type, source, ent)
```

## Match true and predicted entities

```{r match_entities}
# For each paper and entity, flag whether it was annotated (true),
# predicted, or both, and classify it as a TP, FP or FN
matched <-
  ents |>
  mutate(present = TRUE) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = source,
              values_from = present,
              values_fill = FALSE) |>
  mutate(tp = true & predicted,
         fp = !true & predicted,
         fn = true & !predicted)
```

## Calculate precision, recall and F1

```{r prf_function}
# Precision, recall and F1 for each paper, then the median across papers.
# Any existing grouping (e.g. by entity type) is kept, so a grouped input
# gives one row per group.
prf <- function(d) {
  d |>
    group_by(pubmed_id, .add = TRUE) |>
    summarise(across(c(tp, fp, fn), sum), .groups = "drop_last") |>
    mutate(precision = tp / (tp + fp),
           recall    = tp / (tp + fn),
           f1        = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)) |>
    # 0/0 (e.g. no predictions in a paper) counts as 0
    mutate(across(c(precision, recall, f1), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))) |>
    summarise(across(c(precision, recall, f1), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
}
```

```{r prf_results}
# Per entity type
matched |> group_by(type) |> prf()

# All entity types together
matched |> prf()
```

## Figure: performance heatmap

```{r performance_plot, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 6.88}
plot <-
  matched |>
  group_by(type) |>
  prf() |>
  mutate(type = "cohort") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = !type,
               names_to = "metric",
               values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(metric = case_when(metric == "precision" ~ "Precision",
                            metric == "recall"    ~ "Recall",
                            metric == "f1"        ~ "F1")) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = metric,
             x = type,
             fill = value)) +
  # one tile per metric
  geom_tile(colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis",
                       limits = c(0, 1),
                       labels = as.character) +
  # tall colour bar so it spans the tiles
  guides(fill = guide_colourbar(
    theme = theme(legend.key.height = unit(4.5, "in"))
  )) +
  # value printed on each tile
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)),
            colour = "black",
            size = 30,
            size.unit = "pt") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(family = "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next"),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 30, colour = "black"),
        axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 30, colour = "black"),
        legend.box.spacing = unit(30, "pt"),
        legend.margin = margin(r = 0.3, unit = "in"),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(r = 0.3,
                             l = 0.3,
                             t = 0.4,
                             b = 0.4,
                             unit = "in")
  )

plot
```

```{r save_performance_plot}

)
```

# Confusion matrix (all entity types)

## Load the confusion matrix

```{r load_confusion_matrix}
# Rows are true classes, columns are predicted classes; "O" means
# "not an entity"
confusion_mat <- data.table::fread(
  here::here("output/text_mining_predictions/validation_entity_confusion_matrix.csv")
)

# The first column holds the true class labels
names(confusion_mat)[1] <- "true"

# Matrix version, with true classes as row names
confusion_mat_m <-
  tibble::column_to_rownames(confusion_mat, var = "true") |>
  as.matrix()
```

## TP, FP, FN and TN for cohorts

```{r cohort_counts}
true_positives  <- confusion_mat_m["COHORT", "COHORT"]
# true cohorts predicted as some other class
false_negatives <- sum(confusion_mat_m["COHORT", ]) - true_positives
# other classes predicted as cohorts
false_positives <- sum(confusion_mat_m[, "COHORT"]) - true_positives
# everything else
true_negatives  <- sum(confusion_mat_m) - true_positives -
  false_negatives - false_positives

tibble(true_positives, false_positives, false_negatives, true_negatives) |>
  mutate(precision = true_positives / (true_positives + false_positives),
         recall    = true_positives / (true_positives + false_negatives))
```

## Figure: confusion matrix heatmap

```{r confusion_matrix_plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
# Order of classes on both axes
class_order <- c("COHORT", "COHORT_COUNTRY", "OTH_TOOL",
                 "POP_DESC", "REF_PANEL", "O")

# Long format, with the proportion of each true class (row) predicted
# as each class
confusion_mat_long <-
  confusion_mat |>
  pivot_longer(-true, names_to = "pred", values_to = "n") |>
  group_by(true) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(true = factor(true, levels = rev(class_order)),  # rev so COHORT is at the top
         pred = factor(pred, levels = class_order))

ggplot(confusion_mat_long, aes(x = pred, y = true, fill = prop)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  # counts, in white on dark tiles
  geom_text(aes(label = n, colour = prop > 0.5), size = 8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#14828C", limits = c(0, 1),
                      name = "Row\nproportion") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x = "Predicted", y = "True") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 20, angle = 45, hjust = 0),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 20),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 22),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 20)
  )
```
